OmaStats 1.9 lines the bar up on scaled displays, stops polling peripheral batteries every second, which disconnected Apple's Magic Mouse and flooded the kernel log on 2-in-1s, and shows a Mac's fans on the Sensors page.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.9.0/omastats-v1.9.0.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

![The bar in 1.8.1 and 1.9.0 at 160% scaling, enlarged: in 1.9.0 the stacked letters end on the graphs' baselines, the rates sit in the middle of the bar and the graph bars are even, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.9.0/omastats-1.9.0-bar-dark.png)

## New

- **A Mac's fans on Sensors.** On Apple hardware the chassis fans now appear under an SMC chip with their real speed, read from the SMC's ACPI device, and the 0 rpm fan a Mac's built-in graphics card reports is gone. A graphics card in a Thunderbolt enclosure keeps its fans. By @alexhawat (#37).

## Fixed

- **The bar lines up on scaled displays.** At fractional scales such as 160%, the stacked CPU, MEM, NET and DSK letters sat over a pixel low and ended below the graph's baseline, the two-line network and disk rates sat low, and the bars in the bar's graphs came out uneven. OmaStats snapped them to a whole-number pixel ratio and measured the letters in whole pixels. It now uses the display's own ratio, the letters sit in the middle of the bar on the graph's baseline, and the rates are centred by their figures. Nothing changes at 100%. By @crmne.
- **Bluetooth mice stay connected.** Reading a peripheral's battery makes the kernel ask the device, and OmaStats did it every second, which made Apple's Magic Mouse time out and drop its connection. Peripheral batteries are now read every ten minutes, and a failed read is retried after 30 seconds. By @craiutz (#44).
- **No more kernel log flood on 2-in-1s.** A touchscreen that advertises a stylus battery got queried twice a second while no pen was paired, and an ELAN panel answered each query with an error the kernel logged, about 170,000 lines a day. OmaStats now leaves a battery alone while it reports itself absent. By @crmne; thanks @selasi06 (#43).

## Known limitations

- Peripheral battery levels and charging states can be up to ten minutes old.
- Mac fans come from the SMC's ACPI device, where T2 Macs publish them. This was tested on a MacBookPro16,1 only.
- The bar places each readout on whole logical pixels, so at some scales a readout can still sit up to about a device pixel off the bar's centre.
- A laptop's NVIDIA card is read once per idle period (about six seconds) while it is allowed to suspend, so its figures update less often than the rest. This was checked with tests, not on a hybrid laptop: please report how it behaves on yours.
- Without a power supply, battery or platform zone to measure the whole machine, the Power total covers the CPU and GPUs only, not fans, drives or the rest of the board.
- CPU power and its RAPL zones on Intel, and on AMD without integrated graphics, need a udev rule that makes `/sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` readable.
- Power supply readings cover Corsair's USB-connected supplies (the `corsairpsu` driver) only.
- NVIDIA fans report percent of full speed, not rpm, so they do not count towards the Fans ring's average.
- The process search and color fields take typed text only: there is no paste or text selection.
- GPU process lists from open drivers show only your own processes. An integrated AMD card's own load figure jumps between 0% and 100%, so it can disagree with its process list.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.

## Thanks

Thanks @alexhawat for finding where a Mac keeps its fans, @craiutz for tracing the Magic Mouse disconnects to battery polling, and @selasi06 for pinning the touchscreen log flood to the stylus battery.

Both bundled binaries are rebuilt twice in CI, compared byte-for-byte with the committed executables, and covered by checksums and GitHub build attestations.
